The SVD approach is a standard technique in computer vision for averaging rotation matrices, ensuring the result remains in $SO(3)$ [S2, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly describes a process for computing an average camera pose. It states that the method calculates the mean rotation matrix and then performs Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) on it (U, _, Vt = np.linalg.svd(mean_rot)) to calculate the average rotation (avg_rot = U @ Vt). This specific mathematical procedure (U @ Vt from SVD of a mean rotation matrix) is the standard method for projecting a general matrix onto the Special Orthogonal group SO(3) (ensuring orthogonality and determinant +1). Therefore, the evidence supports the claim that SVD is used to average rotation matrices and ensure the result remains in SO(3).
